name: NSW Curriculum 2025
Creative Arts
Year 7 - 10 Dance
Stage 4
describes dance works from a range of contexts using the elements of dance
creates movements using the elements of dance to communicate an idea and intent
performs dance works, demonstrating safe dance practice, dance technique and performance quality
Stage 5
investigates and explains how social, cultural and historical factors shape the development of dance
evaluates dance works based on context, the elements of dance, the dancing body and theatrical elements
creates a movement vocabulary that communicates an idea and intent in response to different contexts
creates movements using the elements of dance and structures movement to communicate a specific idea and intent
demonstrates safe dance practice and dance technique in preparing the body to express and communicate an intent
manipulates the elements of dance to demonstrate performance quality and interpretation in context
Year 7 - 10 Drama
Stage 4
explains how creative choices shape works and experiences through dramatic contexts, processes and elements
creates meaning through experimentation with dramatic contexts, processes and elements

Stage 4
improvises, arranges or composes using the elements of music to create musical ideas
uses listening skills to describe music in relation to stylistic, cultural, historical or social contexts and the elements of music
uses performance skills to demonstrate understanding of the elements of music and communicate musical ideas
Stage 5
improvises, arranges or composes with stylistic understanding and musical expression
manipulates and combines the elements of music to create musical ideas
uses listening skills to analyse music in relation to stylistic, cultural, historical and social contexts
uses listening skills to evaluate how the elements of music are manipulated and combined
performs repertoire with stylistic awareness and musical expression
manipulates and combines the elements of music in performance to communicate musical ideas
Languages
Auslan
Early Stage 1
creates simple texts on known topics using key signs
exchanges meaning using key signs and common protocols
identifies different communication methods
identifies key signs and information and responds in a variety of ways
Stage 1
creates simple informative and imaginative texts on known topics using high-frequency signs
exchanges meaning in guided interactions using high-frequency signs and common protocols
identifies ways of communicating which reflect culture
identifies key information in simple texts and responds in a variety of ways
Stage 2
creates simple informative and imaginative texts on known topics using familiar language
exchanges meaning and information in guided interactions using familiar signs and common protocols
identifies connections between language, culture and identity
identifies key information and some details in simple texts and responds in Auslan and/or English
Stage 3
creates informative and imaginative texts for different audiences using a range of familiar language
exchanges information and opinions using familiar language and protocols for known audiences
describes connections between language, culture and identity
identifies information, opinions and ideas in texts and responds in Auslan and/or English
Stage 4
creates informative and imaginative texts for different contexts and audiences using a range of linguistic structures
exchanges information, opinions and ideas using a range of linguistic structures and protocols appropriate for different audiences
explains the relationship between language, culture and identity
explains how texts represent information, opinions and/or ideas and responds in Auslan and/or English
Stage 5
creates informative and imaginative texts for different contexts and audiences using complex linguistic structures
exchanges information, opinions, ideas and perspectives by manipulating linguistic structures and using protocols appropriate for different audiences
analyses the interrelationship between language, culture and identity
analyses how texts represent information and/or perspectives and responds in Auslan and/or English
Science
Stage 4
Focus Area
explains how energy causes geological and chemical change
describes the unique features of cells in living things and how structural features can be used to classify organisms
explains how data is used by scientists to model and predict scientific phenomena
describes the effects of forces in everyday contexts
describes the role, structure and function of a range of living systems and their components
explains how observations are used by scientists to increase knowledge and understanding of the Universe
explains how uses of elements and compounds are influenced by scientific understanding and discoveries relating to their properties
explains how the properties of substances enable separation in a range of techniques
Working scientifically
Observing: Uses scientific tools and instruments for observations
Questioning and predicting: identifies questions and makes predictions to guide scientific investigations
Planning investigations: plans safe and valid investigations
Conducting investigations: follows a planned procedure to undertake safe and valid investigations
Processing data and information: uses a variety of ways to process and represent data
Analysing data and information: uses data to identify trends, patterns and relationships, and draw conclusions
Problem-solving: identifies problem-solving strategies and proposes solutions
Communicating: communicates scientific concepts and ideas using a range of communication forms
Stage 5
Focus Area
assesses the use of scientific knowledge and data in evidence-based decisions and when verifying the legitimacy of claims
explains how an understanding of the causes of disease can be used to prevent and manage the spread of disease
evaluates current and alternative energy use based on ethical and sustainability considerations
analyses the impact of human activity on the natural world
describes the relationship between the diversity of living things and the theory of evolution
explains how DNA is responsible for the transmission of heritable characteristics and can be manipulated through genetic technologies
assesses the uses of materials based on their physical and chemical properties
describes a range of reaction types
explains the factors that affect the rate of chemical reactions
describes the features and applications of different forms of waves
explains the motion of objects using Newton’s laws of motion
Working scientifically
Observing: selects and uses scientific tools and instruments for accurate observations
Questioning and predicting: develops questions and hypotheses for scientific investigation
Planning investigations: designs safe, ethical, valid and reliable investigations
Conducting investigations: follows a planned procedure to undertake safe, ethical, valid and reliable investigations
Processing data and information: selects and uses a range of tools to process and represent data
Analysing data and information: analyses data from investigations to identify trends, patterns and relationships, and draws conclusions
Problem-solving: selects suitable problem-solving strategies and evaluates proposed solutions to identified problems
Communicating: communicates scientific arguments with evidence, using scientific language and terminology in a range of communication forms

communicates and evaluates design ideas and solutions
